healthcare.costForTourists: Turkey is a major medical tourism destination. Private hospitals are excellent and affordable. Clinic visit $30-60. Private hospital ER $50-200. Istanbul hospitals rival European quality at a fraction of the cost.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Eczane (pharmacies) everywhere, marked with red 'E'. Well-stocked. Pharmacists often speak English. Many medications available without prescription.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Acibadem, Memorial, and Florence Nightingale hospitals in Istanbul are world-class. Antalya and Ankara also have good private hospitals. Eastern Turkey has limited facilities.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance recommended but private healthcare is affordable enough to pay out-of-pocket for minor issues.

controlledSubstances.note: Cannabis is illegal. Even CBD products may cause legal issues.

medications.generalAdvice: Turkish pharmacies are well-stocked and pharmacists are knowledgeable. Bring prescriptions for controlled substances.

scams.name: Shoe shiner drop
scams.description: A shoe shiner 'accidentally' drops his brush in front of you. When you pick it up and hand it back, he insists on shining your shoes out of gratitude, then charges $20-30.
scams.avoidance: Don't pick up dropped brushes. Walk past.

scams.name: Friendly local bar scam
scams.description: A local man befriends you and suggests a 'local bar.' Women appear, everyone orders drinks, and the bill is $500-2,000. Bouncers appear if you resist paying.
scams.avoidance: Never go to bars suggested by strangers on the street. Only visit venues you chose yourself.

scams.name: Carpet/leather shop guided tour
scams.description: Friendly shop workers offer tea and a tour of how carpets/leather are made. What starts as cultural education ends with extreme sales pressure. Prices are inflated 3-10x.
scams.avoidance: It's fine to look and drink tea — but know the real price of Turkish carpets before shopping. Don't feel pressured. 'I'll think about it' is a valid response.

scams.name: Taxi long-route scam
scams.description: Taxi drivers take long routes, especially from airports. Some switch your 50 lira note for a 5 lira note and claim you underpaid.
scams.avoidance: Use BiTaksi app. Monitor the route on Google Maps. Pay with card when possible. Know approximate fares (airport to Sultanahmet: ~150-200 TL).

connectivity.simOptions: Turkcell (best coverage), Vodafone, or Türk Telekom SIM. Tourist SIM packs available at airports $10-20 for 20GB/30 days. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most hotels, restaurants, and cafes. Istanbul has excellent connectivity. Eastern Turkey is spottier.
connectivity.bestOption: Turkcell tourist SIM at the airport.

cultural.tipping: 10-15% at restaurants. Hotel porters 10-20 TL. Tour guides 50-100 TL/day. Taxi: round up.
cultural.dressCode: Women must cover hair, shoulders, and knees at mosques (scarves usually provided at entrance). Remove shoes. Otherwise casual — Istanbul is cosmopolitan.
cultural.greetings: Handshake. Close friends: cheek kisses. 'Merhaba' for hello. Turks are extremely hospitable — expect lots of tea offers.
taboos: Blowing your nose at the dinner table
Refusing offered tea (it's a social bond)
Showing the sole of your shoe to someone
cultural.haggling: Expected at the Grand Bazaar, markets, and some shops. Start at 50% of asking price. Not at restaurants or fixed-price shops.

naturalDisasters: earthquakes (major risk — Turkey sits on active fault lines)
safety.lgbtSafety: Legal but no anti-discrimination protections. Istanbul is relatively tolerant (Beyoğlu/Taksim). Pride parades have been banned since 2015. Exercise discretion outside Istanbul.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe. Some catcalling and unwanted attention, especially in eastern Turkey. Istanbul tourist areas are well-policed. Dress modestly outside tourist areas.
safety.notes: Turkey is safe for tourists. Istanbul is very well-policed. Earthquake risk is significant — know where exits are in buildings. Avoid the Syrian border region.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: e-visa required ($50, 90 days). UK: 90 days visa-free. Some EU: 90 days visa-free.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: April-June and September-November. July-August is hot (35°C+). Istanbul is pleasant year-round. Cappadocia best in spring/fall.
